title: Frozen task / source packet
description: The immutable, revision-bound record of one authoring request: what the author is given, where every fact came from, and whether the request may proceed at all. Version 5 replaces version 4, which was never released. It closes what an independent review found when v4 met real lessons: eight inputs pinned where generation reads ten, rights decided by a class the packet had to infer from an identifier, one host field for five host shapes, a READY status reachable with unresolved facts underneath it, and no place to put the evidence of a refusal that was not also the author’s inbox.

block_reasons.description: Why this packet may not be authored from. Empty exactly when the status is READY.

authorable_packet_ref.description: The authorable packet these bytes are, once it has been written and hashed. Null on every quarantine record: a blocked generation produces no authorable packet, so there is nothing for this to point at.

packet_content_sha256.description: The digest of the authorable packet content. Null on every quarantine record, for the same reason.

identity.description: What this lesson is called and where the curriculum files it. An author who has to infer the title from the identifier is inventing one.

source_sanitization.description: What the generator removed from the source material before the author saw it, counted over the occurrences this packet selected. Version 4 counted over the whole crosswalk, so every packet reported the same number and none reported anything about itself.

allOf.description: A count without its code is a removal nobody can name; a code without its count is a claim with no quantity behind it. Both directions are required, so neither half can stand alone.

input_hashes.description: The ten authoritative inputs, each pinned by the digest of its bytes and by the digest of its canonical content. Ten rows, and one `contains` rule per key below, so the set is exact: `uniqueItems` alone is satisfied by ten rows that name the rubric ten times with different digests.

items.description: One place in one source document, projected to the fields the owner receipt allows for that exact source. There is no field here for source text, which is what makes the prohibition a property of the contract rather than an instruction to the author.

allOf.description: A teachable topic has a scope status; an anchor is a place and has none.

oneOf.description: The attachment hangs off the lesson as a whole: a support artifact, or an extension whose declared cores could not be resolved to this lesson.
Two or more knowledge components of this lesson. A single-element multi is a single, and an empty one is a host nobody named.
This lesson displays an attachment another lesson owns. The owner is named, because a secondary application that does not say what it is secondary to is just an attachment with a missing host.

host_scope.description: What this attachment hangs off, as one of five closed shapes. Version 4 had a singular `host_kc_id`; the curriculum has capstones spanning many components, extensions hosted by capstones, supports attached to a lesson, and attachments displayed in lessons that do not own them. A single field could hold exactly one of those, and the generator had to pick a knowledge component to fill it.

declared_host_core_ids.description: Every host core the curriculum declares for this attachment, preserved verbatim whether or not it resolved. The resolved subset is in `host_scope`; this is the full set, so nothing is lost by resolving.

credits_kc_evidence.description: Whether evidence collected against this attachment may be attributed to a knowledge component. False whenever the host is the lesson, because a lesson-level attachment has no KC to credit.

allOf.description: The id says which family it is, so the kind cannot disagree with it.

A mismatched lineage is carried at lesson level, credits nothing, and says so in words as well as in codes. This is the deadline safe interim: the canonical ids survive, and no KC evidence, exit credit or mastery attribution may derive from them.
A lesson-level or secondary host has no knowledge component to credit.
Only a blocking hold blocks; the classification and the flag agree.

output_requirements.description: Where the work goes and what it is written against. Every value here is a pinned authority or is derived from the lesson id; none of them is a caller’s choice.

provisional_host_lineage.description: Present only when an attachment in this packet carries declared host cores that are not knowledge components of this lesson. The attachment is still delivered, at lesson level, crediting nothing.

allOf.description: READY and AUTHORABLE are the same fact stated twice, and the contract requires them to agree. A READY record on a quarantine surface is a packet somebody can author from that nobody meant to release; a BLOCKED record on an authorable surface is the failure this reconciliation exists to prevent.

A READY packet has no unresolved source anywhere in it. The rule is stated over the whole ordered scope rather than per occurrence, because "one of the twenty is pending" is exactly the case a per-occurrence rule misses.
A packet carrying a provisional host-lineage mismatch says so at the top level too, so a reader who never reaches the attachment list still learns that something in it is uncorrected.
